quote_json: "However, within a single program, no class or struct shall contain more than one method called Main whose definition qualifies it to be used as an application entry point."
notes: 'within a single program, no class or struct shall contain more than one method called Main whose definition qualifies it to be used as an application entry point' (PDF p. 83 lines 23-27), and clause 2 requires at least one diagnostic for a violated 'shall' requirement (PDF p. 17 lines 33-35). Both methods have qualifying signatures (PDF p. 83 lines 6-9), and the per-class rule holds whichever Main the external mechanism selects (PDF p. 83 lines 28-32); the 7th edition's 7.1 drops the per-type cap (PDF p. 69). Renaming the second Main to Spare is the valid witness, isolating the construct; the edition requires a diagnostic and csc gives none. Positive witnesses establish prerequisites; failing originals do not prove mutation sensitivity. At ISO-2, ECMA-334 4th ed 10.1, p. 85 (PDF p. 107) requires this result. The separate selected entry point does not waive the per-type limit. Both carrier variants contain two qualifying Main definitions and require rejection.

quote_json: "Prior to an application\u2019s termination, destructors for all of its objects that have not yet been garbage collected are called, unless such cleanup has been suppressed"
notes: 'Prior to an application's termination, destructors for all of its objects that have not yet been garbage collected are called, unless such cleanup has been suppressed (by a call to the library method GC.SuppressFinalize, for example)' (PDF p. 84 lines 6-8). The sentence is normative, and the 1st edition's latitude covers only the time after eligibility, the order and the thread: 10.9 step 3 says the destructor 'is run' at an unspecified later time (PDF p. 99 lines 39-40), and its 'does not require that destructors be run ... as soon as they are eligible' is timing latitude (PDF p. 100 lines 1-4; also PDF p. 282 lines 10-12 and Annex B.3, PDF p. 380 lines 18-19), never omission at termination, which the 7th edition makes implementation-specific (7.2, PDF p. 71). The test needs Console output to still work while destructors run at shutdown, which the edition's own destructor examples presume (PDF p. 100 lines 8-45), and the suppress=true mutant must stay silent. Positive witnesses establish prerequisites; failing originals do not prove mutation sensitivity. At ISO-2, ECMA-334 4th ed 10.2, p. 86 (PDF p. 108) requires this result. The rooted object has unsuppressed cleanup. The fourth termination rule requires its finalizer before exit even though it is reachable; the hosted runtime omits the required check output.

notes: At ISO-1, a reference to a type's private member made in that type's own attribute section or class-base, outside its body braces, is a compile-time error: [ImprintAttribute(Casket.Code)] class Casket { private const int Code = 31; } and class Vessel : Vessel.ISeal { private interface ISeal {} } are rejected, while the same reference inside the body, or with the member made public, compiles and prints OK 0. At ISO-1, [ImprintAttribute(Casket.Code)] class Casket { private const int Code = 31; } and class Vessel : Vessel.ISeal { private interface ISeal {} } are compile-time errors; the same reference on a member inside the body, or with the member made public, compiles and prints OK 0. At ISO-2, ECMA-334 4th ed 10.5.2, p. 91 (PDF p. 113) requires this result. The access is in a declaration attribute or base list, outside the relevant body braces. Partial-declaration wording does not change these non-partial cases. A protected access outside the program is likewise outside the derived body text; its independently compiled base fixture fixes the assembly boundary.
